newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police detain Kashmiri separatist leader.
newsitem.headline: Indian police detain Kashmiri separatist leader.

text.p: Indian police said on Sunday that they had detained a senior Kashmiri separatist leader after he violated a ban on public gatherings and led a religious procession through troubled Kashmir's largest city.

They said Abdul Gani Lone, a senior leader of All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, was detained along with a dozen supporters after he led a Moharram procession in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
The Hurriyat is an umbrella organisation grouping some 30 leading religious and political groups in Kashmir.
Javid Ahmad Mir, a leader of Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front, was also detained, police said.
Shia Moslems mourn the slaying of a grandson of Prophet Mohammad during the first Islamic month of Moharram.
A police spokesman said the procession led by Lone had violated orders that ban public gatherings of more than four people on the grounds that they may pose a threat to law and order.
Moharram processions and public gatherings have not been allowed in Kashmir since a bloody rebellion broke out in 1990 as they could lead to law and order problems, officials said.
Indian paramilitary troops beefed up security in Shiite dominated areas of Srinagar to prevent any violence, the police spokesman said.
Hurriyat strongly condemned the state authorities for not allowing religous processions and arrest of leaders in Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority region.

"We strongly condemn this act of state authorities, they are not delibertely allowing religous processions and are indiscriminately arresting Hurriyat and religous leaders," Umar Farooq, chairman of Hurriyat said in a statement.
On Friday Moulana Abbass Ansari, a Shia Moslem separatist leader and an executive member of the Hurriyat, was detained by police for leading a Moharram procession in Srinagar.
Ansari is still in police detention.

Over a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in the Himalayan state of Jammu and Kashmir. Police and hospitals say over 20,000 people have been killed in seven years of militancy related violence.
